P03-001.challenge_claim: The unit's onset is carried by an English adversative and by a verse-initial particle the same row refuses to treat as a divider three times inside the span, and the second-person address that opens mid-span is left undisclosed.
P03-001.grounds: Byte-re-derived; both prongs verify and the object, not just the digit, checks out. PRONG 1 (onset argued off the translation layer): the row's onset sentence is the English “But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time, he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time he has made it glorious, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.” (web:Isa.9.1) = oshb:Isa.8.23, and the front verse's Hebrew is never spliced anywhere in the row. That verse in fact opens with the causal particle, כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק לָהּ֒ (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1, byte tier), so the adversative carrying the seam has no counterpart token in the bytes (tier-4 translation layer, never boundary evidence). The same verse-initial particle then stands at כִּ֣י אֶת עֹ֣ל סֻבֳּל֗וֹ (oshb:Isa.9.3 = web:Isa.9.4, byte tier) and opens oshb:Isa.9.4 (= web:Isa.9.5) and oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6) — the three internal sites the row expressly declines to read as boundaries — so one particle carries opposite structural weight at the front seam and inside the span, unargued. PRONG 2 (the unity ground is byte-false): 'without a fresh subject or addressee' fails inside the span. A fresh verse-initial nominal subject stands at הָעָם֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ (oshb:Isa.9.1 = web:Isa.9.2, byte tier); the next verse turns to explicit second-person address, הִרְבִּ֣יתָ הַגּ֔וֹי ... לְפָנֶ֨יךָ֙ (oshb:Isa.9.2 = web:Isa.9.3, byte tier), continued by הַחִתֹּ֖תָ (oshb:Isa.9.3 = web:Isa.9.4, byte tier); and the person does not resume in the birth clause יֶ֣לֶד יֻלַּד לָ֗נוּ (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier), which is third person. Both witnesses render the address alike — “You have multiplied the nation. You have increased their joy. They rejoice before you” (web:Isa.9.3) = oshb:Isa.9.2. What the row gets right stands: the throne-name run, the doubled ketiv/qere pair at oshb:Isa.9.6 (= web:Isa.9.7) with the medial-final-mem ketiv correctly refused as a special-letter seg, the in-span ketiv/qere note at oshb:Isa.9.2 (= web:Isa.9.3), the exegesis note at oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6) named as apparatus, and the setumah at oshb:Isa.9.6 (= web:Isa.9.7) under the correct type (tier-3 parashah, single witness). CALIBRATION NOTE: this row and all eight of its neighbours pass every Tier-0 check clean, so this is an evidence-quality defect in a load-bearing field, not a Tier-0 violation — medium, not high.
P03-001.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field boundary_rationale: (a) replace the English-only onset sentence with a pointed splice of the front verse's opening from oshb:Isa.8.23 (= web:Isa.9.1) at byte tier, and state what distinguishes that verse-initial particle from the three internal sites at oshb:Isa.9.3 (= web:Isa.9.4), oshb:Isa.9.4 (= web:Isa.9.5) and oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6) that the row declines to cut — or drop the particle asymmetry and rest the seam on the scene turn argued from spliced bytes; (b) delete 'without a fresh subject or addressee' and argue the unity on the clause-chaining itself, disclosing the fresh nominal subject at oshb:Isa.9.1 (= web:Isa.9.2) and the second-person address at oshb:Isa.9.2-9.3 (= web:Isa.9.3-9.4) rather than denying them. Field boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Isa.9.1 (= web:Isa.9.2) once it is argued. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): every onset and unity claim in the rewritten rationale carries a byte-tier pointed splice beside its dual-cited ref, no claim of absent subject or addressee survives where the span's own bytes carry one, every zone-A ref keeps its explicit dual, and the row stays clean on ref-validity, mark and web-quote checks.

P03-002.challenge_claim: The fresh-clause onset and the refrain close are byte-clean, but the supporting grammatical-role claim about Ephraim and Samaria is contested in both witnesses, as is its contrast with the preceding unit.
P03-002.grounds: Byte-re-derived; the challenge verifies on the object it names. The onset itself stands and is not contested. What fails is the supporting grammatical-role claim that 'Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria become the addressed object, replacing the royal house of the preceding unit'. The bytes place both names in apposition to the subject of a third-person plural verb: וְיָדְעוּ֙ הָעָ֣ם כֻּלּ֔וֹ אֶפְרַ֖יִם וְיוֹשֵׁ֣ב שֹׁמְר֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.9.8 = web:Isa.9.9, byte tier) — subject-side, neither object nor addressee — and the English agrees, “All the people will know, including Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria, who say in pride and in arrogance of heart,” (web:Isa.9.9) = oshb:Isa.9.8. I independently re-read every verse of the span, from oshb:Isa.9.7 (= web:Isa.9.8) through oshb:Isa.9.11 (= web:Isa.9.12), and confirm no second-person form occurs anywhere in it. The second half of the stated contrast fails too: in the preceding unit the second-person forms at oshb:Isa.9.2 (= web:Isa.9.3) address the giver of the joy, while the royal figure there is third-person throughout, וַיִּקְרָ֨א שְׁמ֜וֹ (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier), so no addressee is being replaced. Severity holds at low: this is a supporting characterisation, not the row's driver — the fresh verse-initial subject at oshb:Isa.9.7 (= web:Isa.9.8) and the refrain close at oshb:Isa.9.11 (= web:Isa.9.12) both verify at byte tier, and the refrain is byte-identical at five verses (sweep: 5 verses, byte tier), so the row's digit and its named earliest site are right. No morphology layer is staged; the person and role claims here are argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings.
P03-002.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field boundary_rationale: replace 'Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria become the addressed object, replacing the royal house of the preceding unit' with the role the bytes carry — an appositional expansion of the subject of the third-person plural verb at oshb:Isa.9.8 (= web:Isa.9.9) — and either drop the contrast with the preceding unit or restate it as a shift of oracle TARGET rather than of addressee. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: no grammatical-role label stands unless the pointed bytes and both witnesses' renderings carry it, and the corrected sentence asserts no second-person form anywhere from oshb:Isa.9.7 (= web:Isa.9.8) through oshb:Isa.9.11 (= web:Isa.9.12), which carries none.

P03-003.challenge_claim: OL: the stanza's only stated onset ground - that no fresh subject reopens - is contradicted by a verse-initial explicit subject in its own first verse and a second subject switch in the next, and the single tier-3 signal at this seam falls after that first verse rather than before it. P03-003.grounds: Both primaries hit this row and their items are DISTINCT defects, not one defect twice; both verify from bytes and both are upheld as stated. OL's item (evidence): the row's only stated onset ground, that no fresh subject or addressee reopens, is byte-false at the span's own first verse — וְהָעָ֥ם לֹא שָׁ֖ב (oshb:Isa.9.12 = web:Isa.9.13, byte tier) is a verse-initial explicit nominal subject, and it is not the subject of the refrain clause it follows, whose subjects are אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ (oshb:Isa.9.11 = web:Isa.9.12, byte tier); the very next verse switches subject again at וַיַּכְרֵ֨ת יְהוָ֜ה (oshb:Isa.9.13 = web:Isa.9.14, byte tier). The cure is not to reverse the boundary: the same referent already carries the preceding stanza at הָעָ֣ם כֻּלּ֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.9.8 = web:Isa.9.9, byte tier), so the discourse continuity the row is reaching for survives — it is the wording that is false, and it understates the row's own front-seam evidence. OL's second prong also verifies: the setumah is keyed AT oshb:Isa.9.12 (= web:Isa.9.13), i.e. the break falls AFTER this unit's first verse, grouping that verse with what precedes; the row discloses it only as an interior break that does not move the close and never notes that it bears against the front seam it sits beside (tier-3 parashah, single witness, never a driver, absence never counterevidence). LF's item (calibration): confidence sits at high for a stanza cut inside the refrain-poem run that the strategy forecasts as an expected low-confidence region, with the 5:25-bridge rival disclosed and undisposed. NEW FINDING that sharpens LF: across the four-stanza run the confidence banding is INVERTED against onset-signal strength — the two stanzas whose onsets carry no fresh signal at all (this row; and the one opening on a particle continuation at oshb:Isa.9.17 = web:Isa.9.18) are rated high with frontier_flag_considered false, while the two that do carry verse-initial onsets (the divine-word dispatch at oshb:Isa.9.7 = web:Isa.9.8 and the woe onset at web:Isa.10.1) are rated medium with the flag true. The weaker-evidence rows are the ones escaping the low-band queue.
P03-003.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field confidence: lower to medium so the band does not exceed the neighbouring stanza's while the same rival is disclosed and undisposed, and set frontier_flag_considered to true with the matching sidecar and frontier-queue rows; if high is kept instead, it must be earned by stanza-specific evidence this stanza's own bytes supply. Field boundary_rationale: replace 'No fresh subject or addressee reopens' with the claim the bytes carry — the verse-initial nominal subject at oshb:Isa.9.12 (= web:Isa.9.13) resumes the same referent already carrying the preceding stanza at oshb:Isa.9.8 (= web:Isa.9.9) — with the pointed splice and the tier named. Field device_notes: add that the setumah keyed at oshb:Isa.9.12 (= web:Isa.9.13) falls after this unit's own first verse, so as tier-3 single-witness corroboration it bears against this front seam rather than for it. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: no 'no fresh subject/addressee' claim survives where the span's first verse opens with one; the mark disclosure states the side the break falls on; the confidence band is not higher than a sibling row resting on strictly stronger onset evidence; mark and ref checks stay clean.

P03-004.challenge_claim: OL: the refrain close and mark disclosure verify, but the seam argument in the rejected alternative places the addressee shift a verse early and calls 'named' a class that neither witness names. LF: confidence sits at high for another stanza cut inside the same refrain poem without a stanza-specific reason for rating above the run's opening stanza.
P03-004.grounds: Both primaries hit this row; the items are DISTINCT. LF's item is UPHELD AS STATED and OL's is REAL BUT MISFRAMED, so the row verdict is refine. LF (calibration): confidence high for a stanza cut inside the same forecast hazard run, with no stanza-specific ground for rating above the run's opening stanza — and this row's own onset is a particle continuation, כִּֽי בָעֲרָ֤ה כָאֵשׁ֙ רִשְׁעָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.9.17 = web:Isa.9.18, byte tier), which the row itself states honestly, so its onset evidence is the weakest in the run while its band is the joint highest; frontier_flag_considered is false here and true on the two medium siblings. The following unit's onset supplies no name — ה֥וֹי הַחֹֽקְקִ֖ים חִקְקֵי אָ֑וֶן (web:Isa.10.1, byte tier) identifies its targets by participial description only, and the English does the same, “Woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees, and to the writers who write oppressive decrees” (web:Isa.10.1); the sibling row arguing that very target calls it 'the unnamed decree-writers', so two rows in one part describe one seam incompatibly. But OL's supporting arithmetic is wrong: the first second-person forms, וּמַֽה תַּעֲשׂוּ֙ (web:Isa.10.3, byte tier), stand TWO verses after the woe onset, not 'one verse further on'. Field confidence: lower to medium with frontier_flag_considered set true and the matching sidecar and frontier-queue rows, or earn high from this stanza's own bytes, which currently open on a particle continuation. P03-006.challenge_claim: The span contains an undisclosed ketiv/qere site, and every seam claim in the row except the woe onset is argued from the English with no Hebrew form behind it.
P03-006.grounds: Byte-re-derived; the challenge is part real, part misread, so it is refined rather than upheld whole. REFUTED SUB-PRONG: 'Assyria's own boastful self-assessment is not what the span opens with' answers a claim the row does not make — the row says the unit RUNS THROUGH the boast, and the bytes bear that out: the divine first-person forms אֲשַׁלְּחֶ֔נּוּ and אֲצַוֶּ֑נּוּ (web:Isa.10.6, byte tier) hold web:Isa.10.5-10.7, and the boast then occupies web:Isa.10.8-10.11, inside the span. The row's rejected alternative refers to the further boast quotation at web:Isa.10.13-10.14, which does follow the span, so it is coherent as written. UPHELD SUB-PRONG: the back seam carries no spliced Hebrew at all — the closing boundary rests entirely on the English of the rhetorical question, whose Hebrew reads הֲלֹ֗א כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֛יתִי (web:Isa.10.11, byte tier); under the standing engagement rule a boundary-relevant claim owes its pointed splice. REFRAMED SUB-PRONG: the in-span ketiv/qere site at web:Isa.10.6 is real — one note, staged as the doubled pair ולשימו וּלְשׂוּמ֥וֹ (web:Isa.10.6, byte tier for the spliced pair; the ketiv member is unpointed and is skeleton grade standing alone) — but no unconditional disclosure debt is owed there: the campaign's unconditional span-relevant symmetry sweep covers petuchah and setumah, while the ketiv/qere arm validates claims that are made, and this row neither counts nor slices in that verse. What is real is within-part inconsistency: the first row of this same stretch discloses its own in-span ketiv/qere site while this one does not. NEW FINDING (stronger than the prong it replaces): the span absorbs an undisclosed tier-1 internal frame — the quotation formula כִּ֖י יֹאמַ֑ר (web:Isa.10.8, byte tier), “For he says, “Aren’t all of my princes kings?” (web:Isa.10.8) — which is where the speaker changes from divine first person to the Assyrian king's quoted boast; the row names neither the frame nor any speech-formula signal key, though the sibling rows in this stretch are held to disclosing internal seam candidates and arguing why they do not cut. Both setumah disclosures (web:Isa.10.4, web:Isa.10.11) verify under the correct type, tier-3, single witness.
P03-006.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). This is a disclosure order only — no boundary change is proposed or authorised here.

P03-007.challenge_claim: An in-span ketiv/qere site is undisclosed, the 'one uninterrupted response' ground passes over an intervening speech in the other mouth and a change in the divine party's grammatical person, and the closing remnant-object claim is made without a pointed form.
P03-007.grounds: Byte-re-derived; the core holds, two supports need correction, so refine. UPHELD: the row's unity ground, that the two therefore-clauses are 'one uninterrupted divine response ... with no addressee change between them', passes over a speech in the other mouth — the quotation frame כִּ֣י אָמַ֗ר (web:Isa.10.13, byte tier), “For he has said, “By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom, for I have understanding. I have removed the boundaries of the peoples, and have robbed their treasures. Like a valiant man I have brought down their rulers.” (web:Isa.10.13) — opening the king's boast between the two clauses; and OL is right that 'no addressee change between them' cannot do the work, since neither clause has an addressee at all, so the stated ground fails to distinguish this seam from any other in the stretch. UPHELD: the closing remnant-object claim in device_notes is asserted with no pointed form, though the verse does carry the plain noun the row names, וּשְׁאָ֥ר עֵ֛ץ יַעְר֖וֹ (web:Isa.10.19, byte tier) — a boundary-relevant claim on that root owes its splice and its tier. CORRECTED: OL's grammatical-person support does not hold as framed. The alternation is already INTERNAL to the first therefore-clause — וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי יְבַצַּ֤ע אֲדֹנָי֙ is third person and אֶפְקֹ֗ד first person in the same verse (web:Isa.10.12, byte tier) — so the third-person stacked title at לָ֠כֵן יְשַׁלַּ֨ח הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת (web:Isa.10.16, byte tier) is not a change ACROSS the clauses and carries no seam weight; if anything it supports the row. CORRECTED: the in-span ketiv/qere site at web:Isa.10.13, staged as the doubled pair ועתידתיהם וַעֲתוּדֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ (web:Isa.10.13, byte tier for the spliced pair), is real, but as at the sibling row no unconditional disclosure debt is owed — the unconditional symmetry sweep is the petuchah/setumah one, the ketiv/qere arm validates claims made, and this row neither counts nor slices there; the finding is within-part inconsistency. NOT CARRYING: the suffixed epithet וּקְדוֹשׁ֖וֹ (web:Isa.10.17, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse) is correctly identified as a DIFFERENT object from the title construct in the next unit's first verse, and because the two are different objects the cross-seam cohesion rule does not trigger — it is an observation, not a defect. Both mark disclosures verify with petuchah at web:Isa.10.19 kept distinct from setumah at web:Isa.10.11 (tier-3, single witness).
P03-007.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 'both continue one uninterrupted divine response to the same quoted boast, with no addressee change between them' with a ground the bytes actually distinguish — the quoted boast in the king's mouth opened by the quotation frame at web:Isa.10.13 sits BETWEEN the two therefore-clauses, so the unity must be argued over that quotation rather than by the absence of an addressee neither clause has; do not rest the replacement on a grammatical-person change across the clauses, since the alternation is already internal to web:Isa.10.12. Field device_notes: splice the pointed remnant noun at web:Isa.10.19 with the tier named instead of asserting the object without a form, and add the in-span ketiv/qere note at web:Isa.10.13 for within-part consistency. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): the replacement ground must DISTINGUISH this seam from the other seams in this stretch — a ground satisfied equally by every neighbouring cut is no ground — and every remnant claim names its object and its tier before any digit.

P03-008.challenge_claim: LF: device_notes misassigns web:Isa.10.22 to the plain-common-noun remnant object when its own letter bytes carry the same two-word collocation that constitutes the name-reactivating clause at web:Isa.10.21. OL: the same misassignment, plus the signature divine title in the unit's first verse engaged only through the English, the throne-name collocation spliced but unremarked, and the back-seam frame named without being quoted.
P03-008.grounds: Both primaries hit this row on the SAME core defect, and both propose the SAME wrong cure, so the row is refined. SHARED CORE (verified, upheld): the row's device_notes groups web:Isa.10.22 with web:Isa.10.20 as 'the plain common noun', but web:Isa.10.22 carries the two-token remnant adjacency שְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב (web:Isa.10.22, byte tier), “only a remnant of them will return. A destruction is determined, overflowing with righteousness.” (web:Isa.10.22), while web:Isa.10.20 carries the bare construct שְׁאָ֤ר יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ (web:Isa.10.20, byte tier) with no adjacent return-verb at all — so the grouping merges two different objects. CORRECTED CURE (both primaries wrong here): neither 'move web:Isa.10.22 into the clause object' (OL) nor 'it is the identical collocation' (LF) is right. The staged device matrix splits this one adjacency into THREE roles across exactly three verses: the son's name at וּשְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב בְּנֶ֑ךָ (web:Isa.7.3, byte tier), the clause REACTIVATING that name at שְׁאָ֥ר יָשׁ֖וּב (web:Isa.10.21, byte tier), and the plain clause at web:Isa.10.22 — and it records the name-versus-clause split as live at exactly this seam. TIER CORRECTION (LF): the two runs are NOT byte-identical to each other — the adjacency reaches 3 verses at skeleton and accent-stripped tier (sweep: 3 verses) and web:Isa.10.21 differs from the other two in accents; at BYTE tier the accented run is shared by web:Isa.7.3 and web:Isa.10.22 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier), so the sign-name's byte twin is web:Isa.10.22, not web:Isa.10.21. OL's further prongs verify: the signature divine title יְהוָ֛ה קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (web:Isa.10.20, byte tier) stands in the unit's own onset verse and is engaged only inside the English quote, with no divine-title object named and no divine_title.* signal key (the bare construct spelling reaches 24 verses at skeleton tier against the staged 25-verse title object, the defective spelling lying outside this stretch); and the spliced אֶל אֵ֖ל גִּבּֽוֹר (web:Isa.10.21, byte tier) goes unremarked though the collocation stands at 2 verses at skeleton tier — here and in the throne names at אֵ֣ל גִּבּ֔וֹר (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier), where the accents differ, so that identity is skeleton, not byte. NEW FINDING: the back-seam argument leans on the following unit's divine-word formula, כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת (web:Isa.10.24, byte tier), yet web:Isa.10.24 is neither quoted nor present in boundary_evidence_refs — the row argues a verse outside its span that it never names at all.
P03-008.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field device_notes: re-cut the remnant-object split to the three roles the staged device matrix carries on this one adjacency — the son's name at web:Isa.7.3, the name-reactivating clause at web:Isa.10.21, and the plain clause at web:Isa.10.22 — and reserve 'plain common noun' for web:Isa.10.20's bare construct, which carries no adjacent return-verb; name the recurrence tier explicitly (3 verses at skeleton tier; the accented run shared by web:Isa.7.3 and web:Isa.10.22 at byte tier). Also in device_notes: name the divine-title object standing at web:Isa.10.20 with its pointed splice rather than leaving it inside the English quote. Field observed_substrate_signals: add a divine_title.* key. Field boundary_evidence_refs: add web:Isa.10.24, and quote the frame the back seam leans on with a pointed splice in boundary_rationale. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): every remnant claim names its object BEFORE any digit, no two of the four objects on this root are merged, the three-way split is not collapsed to two in either direction, every recurrence claim carries its tier, and the ref-mirror stays clean with the back-seam verse present.

P03-009.challenge_claim: LF: the unit's own quoted closing verse is missing from its evidence-reference list, an internal citation gap unlike every other row in this stretch. OL: the messenger frame is correctly owned, but both seams sit on byte-true devices left undisclosed - the divine title stack repeats at byte tier from the verse immediately before the front seam, and the span's own closing verse opens with the in-that-day formula this same stretch elsewhere treats as a unit-opening driver.
P03-009.grounds: Both primaries hit this row with DISTINCT defects; both verify and both are upheld, OL's strengthened by my own re-derivation. LF (citation completeness): the row quotes its own argued close, “It will happen in that day that his burden will depart from off your shoulder, and his yoke from off your neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing oil.” (web:Isa.10.27), but boundary_evidence_refs stops at web:Isa.10.23 and web:Isa.10.24. I checked all nine rows of this stretch mechanically: this is the ONLY one whose own closing verse is absent from its reference list. It is not a mirror violation — the verse is in-span, and the row passes the ref check clean — so it is a completeness defect, not a Tier-0 one. P03-010.challenge_claim: The row leans on a ketiv/qere-bearing verse for its internal mark disclosure without any apparatus disclosure, and rests its closing device on a divine title whose Hebrew object it never names - one the English rendering flattens into the same words as the different stack quoted at the neighbouring seam.
P03-010.grounds: Byte-re-derived; both prongs are real but both need reframing, so refine. PRONG 1 (ketiv/qere): the site is real — MT 10:32 carries one note, staged as the doubled pair inside הַ֣ר בית בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן (web:Isa.10.32, byte tier for the spliced run; the ketiv member is unpointed and is skeleton grade standing alone) — and this row is the strongest of the five such cases in these clusters, because it does not merely contain the verse: it lists web:Isa.10.32 in its own evidence refs and argues from that verse's paragraph mark, engaging the verse while passing over its apparatus. CORPUS EVIDENCE I DERIVED FOR THIS RULING (and which corrects my own earlier framing of this class): across the whole frozen corpus, 43 rows have a ketiv/qere verse inside their span; 35 of them disclose it and 8 do not. Five of those eight sit in these two clusters, and this writer part discloses in only 1 of its 5 such rows, while a sibling part carries the attested formulation for exactly this case — a reference entry reading 'ketiv/qere note, single-witness; content not sliced'. So disclosure of an in-span ketiv/qere verse is settled corpus PRACTICE at a 35-of-43 rate, not merely one part's habit. It is still NOT a Tier-0 debt: the mark-check's unconditional span-relevant symmetry sweep covers petuchah and setumah only, its ketiv/qere arm validates claims that are made, and this row passes every Tier-0 check clean. The primaries reach the right conclusion by the wrong rationale — nothing is 'owed before slicing', because no slicing occurs; what is real is a documented practice deviation. PRONG 2 (divine title): the byte facts verify but the framing overstates. The row does not rest its closing device on a title — its device is the presentative formula, and it splices the Hebrew הִנֵּ֤ה הָאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.33, byte tier) at byte tier, rendered “Behold, the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, will lop the boughs with terror. The tall will be cut down, and the lofty will be brought low.” (web:Isa.10.33). What is real is narrower: the title inside that quoted run is the definite-article stack, a count-object reaching 5 verses at skeleton tier (MT 1:24, 3:1, 10:16, 10:33, 19:4), and it is a DIFFERENT object from אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.24, byte tier; 8 verses at skeleton, and exactly 2 at byte tier) standing at the seam of neighbouring rows — yet both render identically in English, and the row names no title object and carries no divine-title signal key beyond the presentative. The in-chapter recurrence at הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.16, byte tier) is identical to the closing stack at accent-stripped and skeleton tier but NOT at byte tier, and it sits two rows away rather than across this row's own seam, so the cross-seam cohesion rule does not trigger — it is a recurrence to name, not a straddling device. WHAT VERIFIES AND IS NOT CONTESTED: the march onset splice; both parashah claims under the correct type (setumah at MT 10:32 inside the span and setumah at MT 10:34 at its close, tier-3, single witness, no petuchah in the span); treating the place-name sequence as enumeration inside the unit rather than as a list register; and — the row's real strength — disclosing the internal presentative seam candidate AND giving an argued reason to hold the unit across it. SEVERITY: lowered to low. Nothing here is byte-false and no device straddles this row's seam; both prongs are disclosure-register gaps against a seam argument that otherwise verifies.
P03-010.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field boundary_evidence_refs or device_notes: disclose the in-span ketiv/qere note at web:Isa.10.32, using the formulation already attested elsewhere in the corpus for a verse whose letter bytes the row does not slice. Field device_notes: name the divine-title count-object carried inside the quoted presentative run at web:Isa.10.33 — the definite-article stack, distinguishing it from the differently-formed stack standing at web:Isa.10.24 that the English renders identically — and give its tier and digit (5 verses at skeleton tier). Field observed_substrate_signals: keep the presentative key and add a divine_title.* key naming the stack rather than the formula. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: every divine-name engagement names WHICH count-object it engages before any digit, and no title claim rests on an English rendering that flattens two distinct Hebrew stacks; the mark and ref checks stay clean and the existing internal-seam disclosure is preserved intact.

P03-011.challenge_claim: The cut itself is well founded on the bytes, but both structural claims the row offers as its grounds - the stump image answering the felled trees across its front seam, and the closing inclusio - are asserted with no quoted Hebrew form and no tier label, and neither has a byte-level anchor.
P03-011.grounds: Byte-re-derived; the challenge verifies as stated and is upheld. The cut itself is sound and not contested: the onset splice וְיָצָ֥א חֹ֖טֶר מִגֵּ֣זַע יִשָׁ֑י (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier) matches the source bytes and enters a fresh grammatical subject, “A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.” (web:Isa.11.1); the mark layer is right (setumah at MT 10:34, petuchah at MT 11:9, correct types, none inside MT 11:1-11:8, and no ketiv/qere note anywhere in the span, so nothing is owed there). What fails is that both structural claims the row offers as grounds are asserted with no quoted Hebrew form, no tier label and no lexical anchor. FRONT-SEAM CLAIM: the three growth nouns of the onset verse — חֹ֖טֶר (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse), מִגֵּ֣זַע (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses, MT 11:1 and 40:24) and וְנֵ֖צֶר (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier; sweep: 5 verses), the sweeps all at skeleton tier — share no root with the felling vocabulary of MT 10:33-10:34, so the claim that the stump image 'answers' the felled trees is a semantic reading with no byte-level anchor on either side; I independently re-swept all three digits and they hold on the objects named. CLOSING CLAIM: the 'inclusio' names no bracketing term, quotes no form and labels no tier, and the nearest candidate fails — MT 11:9's דֵּעָה֙ (oshb:Isa.11.9, byte tier; that skeleton reaches 8 verses) is not the form attested at MT 11:2, ר֥וּחַ דַּ֖עַת (oshb:Isa.11.2, byte tier; the bare knowledge-noun there reaches 26 verses at skeleton), so no bracket closes at any Hebrew tier. ONE FRAMING NOTE, not adopted and not needed for the defect: the challenge's evidence adds that a semantic continuity across the row's own seam argues against the cut rather than for it. That inference is available but optional — the row can equally be read as disclosing a cross-seam echo, which is the right register; the defect stands either way, because on either reading the claim carries no form and no tier. The back seam is sounder and the challenge says so: the figure does continue into the next verse, מִשָּׁרָשָׁ֥יו (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier) answered by שֹׁ֣רֶשׁ יִשַׁ֗י (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier). Severity low is right: the cut holds; the grounds under it are under-evidenced.
P03-011.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field boundary_rationale: either splice the felling vocabulary from MT 10:33-10:34 beside the growth nouns of web:Isa.11.1 and state the tier at which the two relate — naming it as a semantic, not lexical, echo, since the roots do not meet at skeleton tier — or drop the 'answers the felled trees' sentence and rest the front seam on the fresh grammatical subject, which the bytes already carry unaided. Field boundary_rationale: replace the bare word 'inclusio' either with the bracketing TERM, quoted at both ends with its tier named, or with a plainer closure claim; the knowledge-nouns at web:Isa.11.2 and web:Isa.11.9 are different forms and do not bracket at any Hebrew tier, so they cannot be the unnamed bracket. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): every structural label that names a device — inclusio, echo, bracket — carries a quoted form at each end plus the tier at which the two match, and no boundary-relevant claim stands on an English-only reading; the mark and ref checks stay clean.

P03-012.challenge_claim: OL: the one-verse cut rests on an in-that-day formula that the immediately following verse repeats verse-initially at accent-stripped and skeleton tier, and on a second-time marker that is not that verse's opener, with a two-site banner catchword straddling the same seam undisclosed; also, calling one paragraph-break type the more emphatic of the two is a scribal-convention assertion not sourced from the inventory cited. LF: the named rejected alternative is not clearly the strongest rival, since the verse's own nations/ensign scope continues the preceding unit at least as strongly as it anticipates the regathering oracle, and the coda reading the row's own device notes concede is never adjudicated in that field.
P03-012.grounds: Both primaries hit this row with DISTINCT defects; the core is real but two of the four supports mis-attach and the severity is too high, so refine. UPHELD CORE: the row's sole onset driver recurs verse-initially at the very next verse. MT 11:10 opens וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier) and MT 11:11 opens וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier); I re-derived the tiers directly and confirm they are identical at accent-stripped AND skeleton tier and differ ONLY in accents, so not byte-identical — a tier the row names nowhere. The formula reaches 13 verses at skeleton tier, four of them in this immediate stretch. A driver that both sides of a seam carry cannot by itself mark the seam, and the row neither discloses the recurrence nor labels its tier. ALSO UPHELD, and the cleanest defect here: the row calls one paragraph-break type 'the more emphatic of the two'. That is a scribal-convention ranking sourced from nothing — the single-witness inventory the row cites records type and count only, and the governing addendum requires petuchah and setumah never be conflated while granting no ranking between them. MIS-ATTACHED SUPPORT 1: 'a second-time marker that is not that verse's opener' is a true byte fact — שֵׁנִית֙ (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier) is the sixth token of MT 11:11 — but the DEFECT it names belongs to the sibling row, which presents that run as what opens its unit; THIS row never claims the marker opens the verse, only that it distinguishes the two actions. Against this row the point survives only in a weaker form: the distinguishing token sits after the shared frame, so it cannot carry the seam weight assigned to it. MIS-ATTACHED SUPPORT 2: the banner straddle is real — עֹמֵד֙ לְנֵ֣ס עַמִּ֔ים (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier) and וְנָשָׂ֥א נֵס֙ לַגּוֹיִ֔ם (oshb:Isa.11.12, byte tier) — but the cited two-verse digit belongs to the MT 5:26 and 11:12 pairing, a different object from the 11:10-to-11:12 straddle it is adduced for. On my own sweeps the straddling collocations are 1 verse and 2 verses at skeleton tier respectively, and the bare banner noun is a short-token trap matching 44 verses of mostly unrelated forms — so the straddle must be argued from the attested collocations, never from the bare noun. LF's DISTINCT ITEM, upheld: the formal rejected-alternative field names only the forward fold into the regathering oracle, while the row's own device_notes concedes three readings including the coda reading; the field that must carry the strongest rival never adjudicates the rival the row itself concedes. VERIFIES: both petuchah claims under the correct type (MT 11:9 and MT 11:10), rightly declined as drivers; no ketiv/qere in the span; and the honest medium_low hold with the frontier flag set. SEVERITY: lowered from high to medium — the surviving core is squarely medium, but two supports mis-attach, the row already carries its uncertainty in the right band with the flag set, and every Tier-0 check is clean.
P03-012.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field device_notes: delete the phrase ranking one paragraph-break type as more emphatic than the other — no such ranking is sourceable from the single-witness inventory; keep the type names distinct and unranked. Field boundary_rationale or device_notes: disclose that the in-that-day formula opening this verse also opens the immediately following verse, naming the tier explicitly (identical at accent-stripped and skeleton tier, NOT byte) and the digit (13 verses at skeleton tier), and state what is left carrying the seam once a frame shared by both sides is set aside. Field device_notes: disclose the banner recurrence across the back seam from web:Isa.11.10 to web:Isa.11.12 using the attested collocations with their own digits and tier — never the bare banner noun, whose skeleton is a short-token trap. Field strongest_rejected_alternative: replace or extend it so the rival actually adjudicated is the strongest one the row concedes elsewhere, namely reading this verse as the closing coda of the preceding unit. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: no formula may drive a cut without a disclosed tier and a stated reason it discriminates the seam it draws; every recurrence digit names the object it counts; and the rejected-alternative field carries the rival the row's own notes concede. BOUNDARY NOTE: whether this one-verse unit should stand, fold back, or fold forward is a boundary question reserved to the boss — I considered escalating it and did not, because the defects ruled here are evidence-layer and the row already holds the boundary at medium_low with the rival disclosed. Nothing in this remedy authorises a respan.

P03-013.challenge_claim: The run presented as what opens the unit is mid-verse, while the verse's actual opener is the same formula carrying the boundary at MT 11:10, and the row names only one of the two remnant-root objects that are live in the two verses it cites.
P03-013.grounds: Byte-re-derived; two prongs verify squarely and the challenge is upheld. PRONG 1 (the run presented as the opener is mid-verse): verified and material. The row states that the second-time marker opens the unit and splices יוֹסִ֨יף אֲדֹנָ֤י שֵׁנִית֙ (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier), but that run begins at the FOURTH token; the verse's actual opener is וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier) — which I confirm is byte-identical to the openers of MT 10:20 and MT 10:27 and identical at accent-stripped and skeleton tier to the opener of MT 11:10, the very verse this cut separates from. Meanwhile the row's English quote for the same onset, “It will happen in that day that the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” (web:Isa.11.11), DOES include the formula the Hebrew splice excludes, so the two quotations of one onset disagree about where it begins. PRONG 2 (remnant objects): verified against the staged device matrix, which is decisive here. Both verses the row cites carry TWO of the root's four objects, not one: the plain noun the row names, and the survive-verb it does not — אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִשָּׁאֵר֩ (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier) and לִשְׁאָ֣ר עַמּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשָּׁאֵ֖ר (oshb:Isa.11.16, byte tier), that verb form reaching exactly 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses, MT 11:11 and 11:16, both inside this span), and the matrix independently lists both verses under the verb family. The unnamed object is part of the very noun-plus-relative construction the row treats as its closing echo, so the echo argument runs on an object the row never names. NOT CARRYING: the bare divine name quoted at MT 11:11 belongs to a role-split census, but the row makes no count claim on it, so no count-object naming is owed — an observation, not a defect. NEW FINDING neither primary reports, and machine-confirmed: this row's strongest_rejected_alternative asserts that both halves 'remain governed by the same in-that-day onset with no intervening addressee shift' — a universal claim carrying no adjacent digit-bearing sweep, which the universals check flags. It is one of only two Tier-0 validator flags across all fifteen rows of these two clusters. NEW FINDING: this row sits at high confidence with the frontier flag unset while the sibling row on the other side of the SAME seam holds at medium_low with the flag set and states the boundary is unsettled; two adjacent rows describe one seam with incompatible confidence. VERIFIES: petuchah at MT 11:10 correct type; no petuchah or setumah inside MT 11:11-11:16 (absence never counterevidence); no ketiv/qere in the span; a paseq pair at MT 11:11, single-witness, count-only.
P03-013.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field boundary_rationale: either extend the Hebrew splice to the verse's actual opening tokens so the spliced run matches the English quote already given, or stop describing the mid-verse marker as what 'opens' the unit and describe it as what distinguishes the action inside a frame shared with the preceding verse; whichever is chosen, disclose that the opening frame is byte-identical to the openers at web:Isa.10.20 and web:Isa.10.27 and matches web:Isa.11.10 at accent-stripped and skeleton tier, with the tiers named. Field device_notes: name BOTH remnant objects live in web:Isa.11.11 and web:Isa.11.16 — the plain noun and the survive-verb (2 verses, both in this span) — and re-cut the closing-echo argument so it names the object it actually runs on. Field strongest_rejected_alternative: give the no-addressee-shift claim its adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and unit, or restate it so it carries no universal. Field confidence and frontier_flag_considered: reconcile with the sibling row describing the same seam, or state what this row's own bytes supply that the sibling's do not. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): the Hebrew splice and the English quote for one onset must begin at the same place; every remnant claim names its object before any digit and no two of the four objects are merged or dropped; the universals check returns clean on this row; and no two rows describing one seam carry incompatible confidence without a stated reason.

P03-014.challenge_claim: OL: the twin-onset recurrence claim holds at no Hebrew tier and is quoted only in English, its form-class gloss misnames the difference between the two speaking verbs, an addressee shift at the hymn's own last verse is contradicted rather than disclosed, and the span's ketiv/qere verse is left unchecked. LF: the Yah-plus-tetragrammaton short-form claim is stated as a categorical 'never blended' without the adjacent digit-bearing count the same device notes correctly supply for the twin-strophe claim beside it.
P03-014.grounds: Both primaries hit this row with DISTINCT defects; all the load-bearing prongs verify, so uphold. LF's ITEM, and it is MACHINE-CONFIRMED: device_notes states the short-form stack is 'never blended into the plain tetragrammaton census' — a universal with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep, while the same field two sentences away supplies the sanctioned digit-bearing form for its twin-onset claim. The universals check flags exactly this string; with the sibling flag on the neighbouring row it is one of only two Tier-0 flags across all fifteen rows of these clusters, so LF's own 'low' understates it. OL PRONG 1 (twin-onset recurrence holds at no Hebrew tier): verified by my own re-derivation. MT 12:1 opens וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.12.1, byte tier) and MT 12:4 opens וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֞ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.12.4, byte tier); I compared them at all three tiers and they differ at byte, accent-stripped AND skeleton. Only the in-that-day core matches, and only at accent-stripped and skeleton tier. So 'restates the same onset formula (sweep: 2 verses)' attaches a digit to a formula identity that holds at no Hebrew tier — the count-object is mis-specified, and the row quotes no Hebrew for either onset. OL PRONG 2 (form-class gloss): verified. וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ (oshb:Isa.12.1, byte tier) and וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֞ם (oshb:Isa.12.4, byte tier) are BOTH second person; only number differs, together with the conjunction vowel — so 'differs in person and number' is a byte-checkable claim the bytes contest. OL PRONG 3 (in-span addressee shift): verified, and I can sharpen it. MT 12:6 opens צַהֲלִ֥י וָרֹ֖נִּי יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת צִיּ֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.12.6, byte tier), feminine-singular imperatives with a feminine vocative, continued by the second-feminine-singular suffix בְּקִרְבֵּ֖ךְ (oshb:Isa.12.6, byte tier), against the masculine-plural imperatives הוֹד֤וּ לַֽיהוָה֙ קִרְא֣וּ (oshb:Isa.12.4, byte tier) and זַמְּר֣וּ (oshb:Isa.12.5, byte tier); that feminine imperative reaches 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses, MT 10:30, 12:6, 54:1), and it governs a feminine addressee at צַהֲלִ֥י קוֹלֵ֖ךְ בַּת (oshb:Isa.10.30, byte tier). THE SHARPER POINT, which neither primary draws: the number difference OL identifies in prong 2 IS itself an addressee difference between the two strophes — second-person singular at MT 12:1 against second-person plural at MT 12:4 — so the row concedes the byte feature in device_notes while asserting in the same row that both strophes 'share the same speaker, addressee, and doxological register'. The row contradicts itself across two fields, before the further shift at the hymn's last verse is even reached. OL PRONG 4 (ketiv/qere at MT 12:5): the site is real, staged as the doubled pair מידעת מוּדַ֥עַת (oshb:Isa.12.5, byte tier for the spliced pair), and this row is one of only 8 in the whole corpus that leave an in-span ketiv/qere verse undisclosed against 35 that disclose. But the stated rationale is loose: the row's count claim covers MT 12:1 and MT 12:4, not MT 12:5, so nothing sits 'beneath' it, and no unconditional debt is owed — the unconditional symmetry sweep is the petuchah/setumah one. The prong survives on practice, not on obligation, and does not change the verdict because prongs 1-3 are independently sufficient. VERIFIES: the short-form stack יָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.12.2, byte tier) rightly kept as its own count-object, one of exactly 3 sites; petuchah at MT 12:6 correct type; and the closing title קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.12.6, byte tier) cited only in English, where the plene construct reaches 24 verses at skeleton tier against a 25-verse title object — I re-swept and confirm the 24, the difference being the defective spelling outside this stretch.
P03-014.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field device_notes: give the 'never blended' sentence its adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and unit (the short-form sites and the tetragrammaton census are separate count-objects), or restate it without the universal — the universals check must return clean on this row. Field device_notes: replace 'restates the same onset formula (sweep: 2 verses)' with what the bytes carry — the two onsets are distinct at byte, accent-stripped and skeleton tier, and share only the in-that-day core at accent-stripped and skeleton tier — quoting both onsets in Hebrew and naming the tier and the object each digit counts. Field device_notes: correct 'differs in person and number' to differ in NUMBER (both forms are second person), and then reconcile the consequence — since that number difference is an addressee difference, either withdraw the shared-addressee claim in strongest_rejected_alternative or restate the unity ground on register and speaker alone, and disclose the further shift to a feminine-singular addressee at web:Isa.12.6 with its splice and digit (3 verses). Field boundary_evidence_refs or device_notes: disclose the in-span ketiv/qere note at web:Isa.12.5 in the formulation the corpus already attests. Field device_notes: name the closing divine-title object with a pointed splice rather than English alone. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): no recurrence claim survives without the tier at which it holds; no form-class label survives that the pointed bytes contest; no two fields of one row may assert and concede the same feature in opposite directions; and the universals check returns clean.
